originalTitle: Trump doubles down on Canada trade war as talks remain stalled – US politics live
summary: Trump has imposed 50% tariffs on $20bn in Canadian goods and Canada threatened retaliatory tariffs starting 8 September
content: Democratic lawmakers in the House introduced a war powers resolution on Wednesday seeking to stop the Trump administration’s boat strikes. The US military has killed at least 227 people in 68 strikes in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific since last year as part of a campaign against what it describes as “narcoterrorists” to stop the flow of drugs into the US. The UN and other humanitarian groups have said the attacks are extrajudicial killings. Lawmakers Gregory W Meeks, Adam Smith, Jim Himes and and Bennie G Thompson, the group that introduced the resolution, said in a statement that people have been killed “without due process or a credible national-security justification”. Congress has never authorized the attacks, the group wrote. “A year later, the administration has little to show for this lawless campaign except a mounting body count, a massive price tag, and a stain on the American conscience,” the lawmakers said. “Time and again, this administration has refused to use the military responsibly or consult with Congress, even though the American people have made clear they do not want their tax dollars being spent on more endless military campaigns. It’s time for this failed campaign to end.” The Pentagon has introduced guidelines for the mandatory new ⁠testosterone deficiency screening required for service members age 30 and older, a policy introduced by Pete Hegseth last month. The defense secretary announced the mandate in July, stating that the program would “[ensure] you have the right testosterone levels to operate at your absolute best”. The guidance will go into effect immediately and require testosterone blood tests for men 30 and older. The guidance does not require the tests for younger men or women of any age, though Reuters reports it calls for screening of symptoms, including disrupted menstrual cycles, that are linked to hormonal dysregulation. Doctors have questioned the scientific basis for the policy. Senator Richard Blumenthal has pushed back against a statement from the US Postal Service about its new system to screen millions of mail-in ballots for the upcoming midterm elections. This week it emerged a whistleblower told Congress that the system was hastily thrown together and that a single glitch in scanning could result in whole ballot batches being turned away. Blumenthal said the system, which came after Donald Trump’s executive order tightening federal control over mail-in voting, was “perilously rushed and potentially unlawful”. In response, the postal service said it was “carefully reviewing the concerns”, but that it had spent months developing the federal ballot mail portal and it was done “in a manner consistent with court orders”. Blumenthal said on Wednesday that “absolutely nothing” in the statement “denies or contradicts the deeply disturbing details of the whistleblower’s disclosure”. “Most importantly, it does nothing to directly address the fears of voters that USPS will refuse to deliver their ballots based on the output of a shoddy computer system they started building four months ago,” he said. “‘Just trust us’ is not acceptable.” Congressman James Comer said the US Department of Justice is investigating Ilhan Omar and her “entire family”. In an interview with the rightwing podcaster Benny Johnson, the chair of the House oversight committee referenced a “discrepancy” on a financial disclosure form and said the Minnesota congresswoman was seeking “earmarks for things that would have benefited the Somali community that have already been identified in committing fraud in Minnesota”. Omar has long been the subject of attacks and criticism from the politicians on the right, including JD Vance, who have accused the representative of immigration fraud, among other accusations. The Democrat has also frequently faced xenophobic attacks from Donald Trump. Earlier this year a man sprayed her with vinegar as while was speaking at an event. She told the Guardian in December 2025 that she faced no death threats during Joe Biden’s presidency, but that changed when Trump returned to office. “Now they are back up, and so there is a clear correlation between [Trump’s] presidency and the political violence that we see and the political danger that a lot of members of Congress and electeds feel across the country,” she said at the time. A US judge has blocked Donald Trump’s latest effort to restrict birthright citizenship. Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction, preventing the Trump administration from enforcing the president’s new executive order, which he signed after the US Supreme Court rejected a previous effort. The new order targets so-called “birth tourism”, and seeks to make children of people who work for foreign governments and those classified as an “alien enemy”, among other groups, ineligible for automatic citizenship. Boardman said the order was “almost certainly unconstitutional”. “This Court must, once again, preliminarily enjoin enforcement of the President’s most recent attempt to strip the right to citizenship from them,” she wrote. Patagonia, the outdoor clothing and gear company, has joined a lawsuit challenging Donald Trump’s decision to significantly reduce the Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments in Utah, removing protections from nearly 3m acres. In July, the president approved the reduction of the sites by 90%, clearing the way to open the land to oil and gas companies. He argued in his proclamations that doing so would allow lands to be “put to a higher-priority use” and that they contained critical minerals important to “ resource independence …[and] national security”. chineseSummary: 特朗普对价值 200 亿美元的加拿大商品征收 50% 关税，加拿大威胁从 9 月 8 日开始征收报复性关税
chineseContent: 众议院民主党议员周三提出了一项战争权力决议，寻求阻止特朗普政府的船只袭击。自去年以来，美国军方在加勒比海和东太平洋地区发动了 68 次袭击，造成至少 227 人死亡，这是打击所谓“毒品恐怖分子”、阻止毒品流入美国的行动的一部分。联合国和其他人道主义组织表示，这些袭击是法外处决。提出该决议的议员格雷戈里·W·米克斯、亚当·史密斯、吉姆·希姆斯和本尼·G·汤普森在一份声明中表示，有人被杀害，“没有正当程序或可信的国家安全理由”。该组织写道，国会从未授权发动袭击。议员们表示：“一年后，除了不断增加的死亡人数、巨大的价格标签和美国良知上的污点之外，政府在这场无法无天的运动中几乎没有什么可展示的。” “本届政府一次又一次拒绝负责任地使用军队或与国会协商，尽管美国人民已经明确表示，他们不希望自己的税款被花在更多无休止的军事行动上。现在是结束这场失败的军事行动的时候了。”五角大楼推出了对 30 岁及以上军人进行强制性新睾酮缺乏症筛查的指导方针，这是皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 上个月提出的一项政策。国防部长于 7 月宣布了这项授权，并表示该计划将“[确保]你拥有适当的睾丸激素水平，以达到最佳状态”。该指南将立即生效，并要求 30 岁及以上的男性进行睾酮血液检测。该指南并不要求对任何年龄的年轻男性或女性进行测试，尽管路透社报道称该指南要求进行 SCR
